title: Cloud-Based Quantum Computing for Biological Network Analysis
author: Weidner, Rossini, et al.
materials: In the following we explain how to set up an account and the required instance to send tasks to these devices.1.Go to the registration portal at https://cloud.ibm.com/registration?target=%2Fquantum.2.Follow the steps the portal requires:a.Provide a valid e-mail and password for the new account and verify the account.b.Provide required information regarding billing details, then confirm the provided bank account by accepting a billing request for 0,00$ which serves to check the validity of the provided credit card.Note: At the time of publication, IBM is offering a free trial of up to $200 worth of simulation time on the platform, valid for 35 days. However, this is listed as a special limited time offer.3.Once logged in, go to the webpage https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/apikeys. There, to create the API key needed to log in to the IBM services through Qiskit, follow these steps:a.Press “Create” on the blue button at top right of the table as in Figure 1.Figure 1Snapshot of the API key interface of the IBM Quantum cloudb.Add a name and a description for the API key to be created, then press on the blue button “Create”.Note: This key uniquely identifies a user and will be required later in step 5a. For further documentation on API keys for IBM Cloud services, please check at https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/app-connect/container?topic=servers-creating-cloud-api-key.c.The API key can be retrieved from the page that opens right after the one shown in Figure 2, as shown in Figure 3:Optional: Here one can visualize the API key by pressing on the eye-shaped icon, then copy or download it by using the two buttons on the lower right corner. The downloaded file is a .json formatted text which can be opened by a text editor as shown in Figure 4CRITICAL: It will not be possible to retrieve this code from the website, so it is crucial to save it in a secure place! Furthermore, it is strongly suggested to keep this identifying code private, as they allow for interaction with IBM services. The posting of this information on open-source platforms such as GitHub repositories could be an opportunity for account theft.Figure 2Snapshot of the API key creation interface of the IBM Quantum cloudFigure 3Snapshot of the interface needed to retrieve the API key on the IBM Quantum cloudFigure 4Snapshot of the .json file containing the API key, opened on the Windows text reader4.The next step is to create an instance and retrieve from there the required CRN (Cloud Resource Name) for the login. To create the CRN:a.Go to the following webpage: https://cloud.ibm.com/quantum/instances and press on the “Create instance” blue button. This redirects you to a different webpage.b.In the new page, select the price plan required. The Lite plan, with free access, allows us to access only to the quantum device simulators. To access to the real devices, select the Standard plan (see red box in Figure 5).Figure 5Snapshot of the webpage dedicated to the creation of an instance on the IBM Quantum Cloudc.Check on the green highlighted box to accept license agreements.d.Click on the blue “Create” button.e.In the following page you can retrieve your CRN as shown in Figure 6, highlighted in green. This code, together with the API key retrieved before, will be used in step 5a.Figure 6Snapshot of the webpage where the CRN code can be retrieved, in the green boxNote: This code serves as a globally unique identifiers for cloud resources. For further documentation on the role of CRNs for IBM Cloud computing, please check https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/account?topic=account-crnCRITICAL: The red-highlighted box in Figure 6 shows where to set a time limit for the computation run on the quantum device. Remember to set a time limit according to your needs to avoid unnecessary costs due to coding or algorithmic errors!5.Now we connect to the IBM instance we just created from our notebook (STARProtocol.ipynb), accessing the computational resources we need. To do so:a.Save on disk the account credentials using the following code (you need to insert in quotation marks the API key from step 3c and the CRN from step 4e):apikey = "ENTER-YOUR-IBMCLOUD-API-KEY"crn = "ENTER-YOUR-INSTANCES-CLOUD-RESOURCE-NUMBER"name = "StarProtocol"# Save an IBM Cloud account on disk and give it a name.QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(channel="ibm_cloud", token=apikey, instance=crn, name=name)b.Connect to the service by calling the account as follows:service = QiskitRuntimeService(name="StarProtocol")

steps.title: Create IBM Cloud account
steps.instruction: Visit https://cloud.ibm.com/registration?target=%2Fquantum, provide a valid e‑mail and password, verify the e‑mail, enter billing details and confirm the $0.00 verification charge; note that IBM offers a free trial of up to $200 for 35 days. Estimated time: 30–45 min.

substeps.instruction: Open registration portal and fill e‑mail/password.
Enter billing information and accept $0.00 verification charge.

steps.title: Generate IBM API key
steps.instruction: After logging in, go to https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/apikeys, press the blue “Create” button, give the key a name and description, create it, then copy the displayed API key or download the .json file; store the key securely because it cannot be retrieved later.

substeps.instruction: Create the key and copy or download it.
Save the key in a secure location.

steps.title: Create IBM Quantum instance & get CRN
steps.instruction: Open https://cloud.ibm.com/quantum/instances, click “Create instance”, choose a price plan (Lite for simulators, Standard for real devices), accept the license agreement, create the instance, then retrieve the Cloud Resource Name (CRN) shown in green; set a time limit for runs to avoid unnecessary costs. Estimated time: 30–45 min.

substeps.instruction: Go to the instance creation page.
Accept license and create the instance.

steps.title: Save IBM credentials in notebook
steps.instruction:
In your Jupyter notebook, assign variables:
```python
apikey = "ENTER-YOUR-IBMCLOUD-API-KEY"
crn    = "ENTER-YOUR-INSTANCES-CLOUD-RESOURCE-NUMBER"
name   = "StarProtocol"
```
Then run:
```python
QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(channel="ibm_cloud", token=apikey, instance=crn, name=name)
service = QiskitRuntimeService(name="StarProtocol")
```

substeps.instruction: Define apikey, crn, and name variables.
Connect to the service with QiskitRuntimeService.

steps.title: Confirm IBM setup ready
steps.instruction: All IBM Cloud resources are now configured; you can run algorithms on a simulator or on a real quantum device.

steps.title: Create AWS account for Braket
steps.instruction: Go to https://portal.aws.amazon.com/billing/signup#/start/email, provide a valid e‑mail, account name, verify the e‑mail with the code, set a password, enter personal and bank details, verify the bank account and identity, select basic support, and log in. Estimated time: 45–60 min.

substeps.instruction: Open AWS sign‑up page and enter e‑mail and name.
Enter personal and banking information and verify.
Choose basic support and complete registration.
Log in to the new AWS account.

steps.title: Create S3 bucket for Braket
steps.instruction: Navigate to https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/get-started?region=us-east-1, click “Create bucket”, name it starting with “amazon‑braket‑<your‑name>”, keep default settings, and create the bucket.

steps.title: Create folder in bucket
steps.instruction: Open the newly created bucket, click “Create folder”, give the folder a meaningful name (this folder will store all IonQ computation results), and record the folder name for later use in the notebook.

substeps.instruction: Save the folder name for notebook use.

steps.title: Generate IAM access keys
steps.instruction: Go to https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam, click “Users”, add a new user (if none exists) with a chosen username, keep default permissions, create the user, select the user, open “Security credentials”, click “Create access key”, choose “Other”, optionally add a tag, create the key, then copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key (download the .csv file); store them securely because the secret is shown only once.

substeps.instruction: Add a new user and set username.
Proceed with default options and create user.
Select the user and open Security credentials.
Optionally tag the key and create.
Copy Access Key ID and Secret Access Key or download .csv.

steps.title: Install and verify AWS CLI
steps.instruction: Download the AWS CLI for your operating system from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html#getting-started-install-instructions, install it following the provided instructions, then open a terminal or PowerShell and run `aws --version` to confirm successful installation.

substeps.instruction: Install the CLI per OS instructions.

steps.title: Configure AWS CLI with credentials
steps.instruction: Run `aws configure` in a terminal and, when prompted, enter the Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, default region name (the region shown on the bucket page), and optionally a default output format. This stores the credentials locally for later use.

steps.title: Review IonQ pricing
steps.instruction: Remember that the IonQ Harmony processor costs $0.30 per task plus $0.01 per shot (each circuit execution).

steps.title: Proceed to Boolean network analysis
steps.instruction: With IBM and IonQ accounts fully configured, you can now start the analysis of Boolean networks using the provided STARProtocol notebook.

description: Before describing the creation of quantum circuits for analyses of logical networks, we show the account setup process for obtaining access to cloud-based quantum processors. As the account setups are now complete, you can begin with the analysis of Boolean networks.
